qs.q: Why is fluconazole recommended over topical therapy for patients with oral candidiasis who have a CD4 count less than 100 cells/microL?
o: To prevent the development of esophageal candidiasis
To completely eradicate mucosal HIV reservoirs
To avoid all drug interactions with HAART regimens
To reverse established villous atrophy in the small bowel
qs.e: Fluconazole is recommended over topical therapy in patients at risk of esophageal candidiasis, specifically those with a CD4 count under 100 cells/microL. Topical agents have no role in esophageal disease.

qs.q: A 30-year-old man has weight loss, chronic diarrhea, then develops Pneumocystis pneumonia, CMV retinitis, and oral candidiasis. Most likely lab finding?
qs.e: Multiple opportunistic infections (Pneumocystis, CMV, Candida) = AIDS. CD4 count below 200/microliter is the threshold at which AIDS-defining opportunistic infections occur in HIV infection.
